findings.finding_text: Attrition is measured night-by-night rather than cumulatively across the block, and liability is triggered whenever a given night's occupancy falls below 90% of that night's block — far more aggressive than CD's 70% cumulative threshold. Unoccupied rooms are charged at 90% of the group rate (versus CD's 70%), and the Hotel's own reservation records are the sole basis for calculation without a true audit right (the Hotel only agrees to produce records within 20 business days on request, and disputes must be raised within 60 days or are waived). The 95%-occupancy full-credit provision is present and matches CD's standard, but it doesn't offset the much harsher core mechanism.
findings.cd_standard: Attrition should be measured cumulatively across the entire room block, not night-by-night, with liability triggered only if pickup falls below 70% of the block. For each unsold room night below that threshold, Group should pay 70% of the group rate, not 90%. Group should have a formula-based, not discretionary, damages calculation and real audit rights.
findings.proposed_language: Attrition liability, if any, will be calculated on a cumulative (not night-by-night) basis, with liability triggered only if Group's actual pickup falls below seventy percent (70%) of the total contracted room block across the Event. For each unsold room night below that threshold, Group will pay an amount equal to seventy percent (70%) of the confirmed group room rate (plus applicable tax). For any night the Hotel achieves 95% occupancy or higher, Group will receive full credit toward its block commitment for that night. At Group's request, Hotel will provide supporting occupancy records within a reasonable time (not to exceed 10 business days) to verify the calculation.
findings.quoted_text: Attrition is measured on a night-by-night basis, and the Group's block commitment is deemed satisfied only to the extent that occupied rooms meet or exceed ninety percent (90%) of the rooms reserved for each night of the Event.
findings.exposure_basis: Difference between billing shortfall at 90% vs 70% of group rate: 95 rooms x $168 x 20% difference = $3,192/night worst case per night if entire night unsold; illustrative based on full block size and rate differential, not a specific shortfall scenario.

findings.finding_text: Cancellation damages are calculated on gross room revenue rather than room profit (70% of group rate), and the Hotel has no obligation to mitigate: resale revenue from cancelled rooms is retained entirely by the Hotel with no credit to Group, and rebooking within a year does not offset damages owed. The sliding scale percentages (35% to 70%) are also applied to full gross revenue, not a mitigated profit figure, materially increasing Group's exposure.
findings.cd_standard: Cancellation damages should be calculated against lost room profit (70% of group rate), not gross revenue, with the hotel obligated to actively mitigate by reselling cancelled rooms and crediting proceeds, and a credit toward damages if Group rebooks within a reasonable window.
findings.proposed_language: Liquidated damages will be calculated as a percentage (per the sliding scale) of room profit — defined as seventy percent (70%) of the confirmed group room rate — rather than gross room revenue. Hotel will undertake reasonable efforts to resell cancelled rooms and food and beverage functions, and will credit those resale revenues, less substantiated transaction costs, against the cancellation fee. Should Group rebook the Hotel for another meeting within one (1) year of the cancellation, Hotel will credit 100% of the room revenue generated by that rebooking toward the damages owed, up to the amount of damages paid.
findings.quoted_text: Group shall owe liquidated damages calculated as a percentage of gross room revenue that would have been earned on the cancelled or reduced rooms, based on the nightly group rates in effect at the time of cancellation.

findings.finding_text: The contract expressly states that resale revenue from cancelled rooms is retained entirely by the Hotel with no credit applied against Group's liquidated damages, contrary to CD's standard requiring mitigation and crediting of resale proceeds.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should have an affirmative, documented duty to try to resell cancelled rooms and functions, and credit those proceeds against whatever the group owes, with records available to verify the effort.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will undertake all reasonable efforts to resell cancelled rooms and food and beverage functions, and will credit those revenues, less reasonable, substantiated transaction costs, against any cancellation or attrition damages owed by Group, not to exceed the full amount of such damages. Sales logs and occupancy records documenting this mitigation effort will be made available to Group upon request.
findings.quoted_text: Any revenue the Hotel generates by reselling rooms within the cancelled portion of the Group's block shall be retained by the Hotel with no credit applied against the Group's liquidated damages obligation.

findings.finding_text: The 30-day cutoff falls within CD's acceptable 21-30 day range, and post-cutoff reservations remain available at the group rate subject to availability, which aligns with CD's position; however, the clause explicitly excludes any post-cutoff reservations from counting toward attrition credit, which somewhat undercuts Group's ability to mitigate its own attrition exposure.
findings.cd_standard: The room block cutoff date should be no earlier than 21-30 days prior to arrival, and reservations after cutoff should remain available at the group rate subject to availability rather than automatically reverting to rack rate.
findings.proposed_language: Reservations made after the cutoff date, to the extent accommodated by Hotel at the group rate, shall be credited toward Group's block commitment and pickup for attrition calculation purposes.
findings.quoted_text: such reservations shall not be credited against the Group's block commitment for purposes of attrition calculation

findings.finding_text: The contract contains no provision addressing the Hotel's obligations if it walks (relocates) a guaranteed reservation due to overbooking.
findings.cd_standard: If the hotel walks a guaranteed reservation, it should provide comparable-or-better accommodations, round-trip transportation, message-forwarding, an upgrade and welcome amenity on return, and credit the relocated night toward Group's pickup and commission — with no attrition liability to Group for any relocated night.
findings.proposed_language: If the Hotel is unable to accommodate any guest holding a confirmed reservation, the Hotel will, at its own expense: (a) provide accommodations at a comparable or better hotel as close as possible for each night the guest is displaced; (b) provide complimentary round-trip ground transportation between the Hotel and the alternate hotel; (c) forward the displaced guest's telephone messages and mail; and (d) upon the guest's return, provide upgraded accommodations if available and a welcome amenity from the General Manager. Each displaced room will be credited toward Group's final pickup and remain commissionable, and Group will not be liable for attrition damages for any night a guest is relocated.

findings.finding_text: The contract does not address what happens if the Hotel undergoes a change in ownership, management, or brand affiliation, or files for bankruptcy or foreclosure, prior to the Event.
findings.cd_standard: If the hotel changes brand, management company, or ownership — or files for bankruptcy or foreclosure — before the event, the hotel should be required to notify the group within 30 days, and the group should be able to terminate without liability within 30 days of that notice, with a prompt refund.
findings.proposed_language: Should Hotel undergo a material change in ownership, management company, or brand affiliation, or file for bankruptcy, or have foreclosure occur, Hotel will inform Group in writing within thirty (30) days of such change or filing. Group may, at its sole discretion, terminate this Agreement without liability within thirty (30) days of receiving that notice. Hotel will refund all deposits and prepayments made by Group within five (5) business days of the notice of termination.

findings.finding_text: The contract contains no representation regarding current or planned renovation, and no notice or termination rights if renovation is later confirmed that would interfere with Group's event.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should represent it has no current renovation plans affecting the group's space, and commit to 30 days' written notice of any renovation confirmed after signing, with a right for the group to terminate without liability if it will interfere.
findings.proposed_language: As of the date of this Agreement, Hotel has no plans for renovation or remodeling of any facilities to be used by Group, other than ordinary maintenance. If Hotel later confirms any such plans, Hotel will notify Group in writing within thirty (30) days, describing the scope, schedule, anticipated impact, and mitigation plan. If Group determines the work will interfere with its meeting, Group may terminate this Agreement without liability upon written notice given within thirty (30) days of receiving Hotel's notice.

findings.finding_text: San Antonio, Texas is within a region subject to tropical storm/hurricane activity, and the contract has no separate named-storm cancellation provision distinct from the general force majeure clause.
findings.cd_standard: In coastal and hurricane-belt markets, force majeure language is often supplemented by a separate, narrower named-storm clause with its own notice period and cancellation window.
findings.proposed_language: In the event a named storm (hurricane, tropical storm) is forecast to affect the Hotel's location within 72 hours of any event date, either party may cancel the affected portion of the event without liability upon written or verbal (followed by written) notice, regardless of whether the storm ultimately causes physical damage to the Hotel.

findings.finding_text: The contract does not address restrictions on the Hotel's use of Group's rooming list or attendee data for its own marketing purposes or disclosure to third parties.
findings.cd_standard: Rooming list and attendee data provided to the hotel should not be used by the hotel for its own marketing or sold to third parties without the group's consent.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will use rooming list and attendee data solely for the purpose of fulfilling reservations under this Agreement. Hotel will not use such data for its own marketing purposes, nor disclose it to any third party, without Group's prior written consent.

findings.finding_text: The contract contains no warranty of ADA compliance for guest rooms, common areas, function space, or transportation, and no allocation of responsibility for auxiliary aids.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should warrant that its guest rooms, common areas, function space, and transportation services comply with ADA public accommodation requirements, with each party indemnifying the other only for its own ADA obligations and a clear division of who funds auxiliary aids.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel warrants that its guest rooms, common areas, function space, and transportation services comply with the public accommodation requirements of the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA). Hotel and Group will each indemnify and hold harmless the other from liability arising from that party's own obligations under the ADA. Group is responsible for obtaining and funding any auxiliary aids needed in the function space held for its use; Hotel is responsible for obtaining and funding any auxiliary aids required by law in guest rooms, public space, and common areas.

findings.finding_text: The contract contains no provision requiring the Hotel to disclose collective bargaining agreement expiration dates or notify Group of labor disputes, and no right for Group to cancel without liability if a strike or lockout arises near the Event.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should give a year's advance notice of when its collective bargaining agreements expire, and prompt notice of any actual labor dispute. If a strike, lockout, or expired contract arises within 90 days of the event, Group should be able to cancel with no liability.
findings.proposed_language: One year in advance, Hotel will provide Group in writing a list of all collective bargaining agreement expiration dates for the ensuing year. Hotel will notify Group in writing within ten (10) working days after becoming aware of any labor dispute involving Hotel's employees. If, within ninety (90) days prior to or during the Event, Hotel's contract with its union employees has expired, picketing occurs, or a strike or lockout occurs, Group may cancel this Agreement by written notice without liability, and any deposits or payments made by Group will be promptly refunded.

findings.finding_text: The contract does not guarantee that the Hotel will refrain from selling rooms to the general public at a rate lower than Group's contracted group rate during the Event dates, nor provide for a rate adjustment if it does.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should guarantee it won't sell rooms to the general public at a lower rate than the group's contracted rate during the event dates, and adjust the group's rate to match if it does, including retroactively.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel guarantees it will not sell guestrooms at a rate lower than Group's contracted group rate of $168.00 during the Event dates, with the exception of qualified rates (e.g., government, airline crew). If Hotel offers a lower guestroom rate, Hotel will adjust the rate for all prior reservations in Group's block to match, and such rooms remain fully commissionable and creditable toward Group's pickup and any attrition calculation.

findings.finding_text: The contract does not distinguish between gratuity (distributed to staff) and any separate service charge (retained by the Hotel), nor require disclosure of the applicable percentages.
findings.cd_standard: Gratuity and service charge should be clearly and separately defined: gratuity fully distributed to staff, service charge disclosed as hotel revenue, not left ambiguous.
findings.proposed_language: Any gratuity charged to Group's account will be fully distributed to the servers, and where applicable, bussers and bartenders assigned to the Event. Any service charge is separate from gratuity, is not distributed as a tip, and is retained by Hotel. Both charges, and their respective percentages, will be disclosed to Group in writing prior to the Event.

findings.finding_text: The contract does not provide for weekly pickup reports before cutoff, a post-event report within 30 days of departure, or a no-cost room-block audit comparing the Hotel's in-house guest list against Group's registration list.
findings.cd_standard: Group should get a weekly pickup report starting before cutoff, a full post-event report within 30 days of departure, and a no-cost room-block audit right with miscoded rooms credited to Group's pickup.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will provide Group a weekly guestroom pickup report starting fourteen (14) days prior to the cutoff date, and a full post-event report — including rooms actualized, suite and double-occupancy usage, and a food and beverage revenue recap — within thirty (30) days of Group's departure. At Group's request, Hotel will conduct a face-to-face room block audit at no cost, comparing the Hotel's in-house guest list against Group's registration list. Any guest room occupied by an individual on Group's registration list but not coded to Group within Hotel's system will be credited to Group's final pickup regardless of the rate paid.

findings.finding_text: The contract contains no provision permitting Group to assign the Agreement to a successor management company or affiliated entity without the Hotel's consent.
findings.cd_standard: The group should be able to assign the contract to a successor management company or affiliated entity without the hotel's consent being unreasonably withheld, particularly where the event itself is unchanged.
findings.proposed_language: Group may assign this Agreement to a successor association management company or affiliated entity without Hotel's consent, provided the assignee assumes all obligations under this Agreement and the event dates, room block, and program remain substantially unchanged. Any other assignment requires Hotel's consent, not to be unreasonably withheld.

findings.finding_text: The finance charge on undisputed unpaid balances compounds monthly rather than accruing simply, which increases the effective annual rate above CD's flat 1%-per-month cap standard.
findings.cd_standard: A finance charge on a late, undisputed balance should be capped at 1% per month or the legal maximum, whichever is less — implying simple, not compounding, interest.
findings.proposed_language: In the event any balance remains unpaid after thirty (30) days from invoice date, the Hotel shall assess a finance charge not to exceed one percent (1.0%) per month, or the maximum allowed by law, whichever is less, applied on a simple (non-compounding) basis to the unpaid, undisputed balance.
findings.quoted_text: the Hotel shall assess a monthly finance charge of one percent (1%) on the unpaid balance, compounding monthly until paid in full

analysis.document_notes: The contract is otherwise clearly drafted and well-organized with numbered sections. Several clauses (force majeure, termination for cause, mandatory fees, complimentary rooms, security deposit, outside vendors, F&B minimum, governing law/venue) closely track or exceed CD's standard positions and are not flagged below. The most significant deviations are in the attrition and cancellation damages clauses, which together represent the largest financial exposure in the agreement. A number of standard CD clauses (walk/relocation, ADA, named storm, labor disputes, rate parity, gratuity/service charge disclosure, assignment, data handling, renovation notice, brand/ownership change, audit/reporting rights) are absent entirely and should be proposed as additions.

findings.finding_text: Attrition threshold is set at 75% pickup and damages at 75% of ADR, rather than CD's standard 70% threshold and 70% rate. This raises Group's liability exposure both by lowering the cushion before damages kick in and by increasing the per-room-night rate charged.
findings.cd_standard: Attrition liability should trigger only below 70% cumulative pickup, with damages calculated at 70% of the group rate, not a higher threshold or rate.
findings.proposed_language: Attrition liability, if any, will be triggered only if Group's actual cumulative pickup falls below seventy percent (70%) of the total contracted room block. For each unsold room night below that threshold, Group will pay an amount equal to seventy percent (70%) of the confirmed group room rate (plus applicable tax).
findings.quoted_text: If Group fails to occupy at least seventy-five percent (75%) of the room block reserved for the Event, Hotel shall assess attrition damages against Group in accordance with the provisions of this clause.

findings.finding_text: No mechanism is stated crediting excess F&B revenue against room attrition damages (or vice versa), which CD's standard calls for as an offset.
findings.cd_standard: Any excess food and beverage revenue above Group's F&B minimum should be credited against room attrition damages, and vice versa.
findings.proposed_language: Any excess food and beverage revenue above Group's F&B minimum will be credited against room attrition damages, and vice versa.

findings.finding_text: The cutoff date is set at 32 days prior to arrival, slightly beyond CD's recommended 21-30 day window, giving the hotel a longer window before the group rate protection applies and slightly reducing Group's flexibility for late bookings.
findings.cd_standard: The room block cutoff date should be no earlier than 21-30 days prior to arrival.
findings.proposed_language: Group shall provide the Hotel with a final rooming list no later than twenty-one (21) days prior to the Event's opening day.
findings.quoted_text: Group shall provide the Hotel with a final rooming list containing all guest names, room type preferences, and arrival and departure dates no later than thirty-two (32) days prior to the Event's opening day.

findings.finding_text: Post-cutoff reservations are only offered at the group rate on a discretionary, yield-management basis rather than a firm commitment subject to availability, undermining the group rate protection CD requires.
findings.cd_standard: After the cutoff date, the Hotel should continue to accept reservations at the group rate on a space-available basis, not subject to yield-management discretion.
findings.proposed_language: After the cutoff date, the Hotel will continue to accept reservations at the group rate on a space-available basis.
findings.quoted_text: Pricing and room type availability following the cutoff shall be determined solely by Hotel's yield management practices and current market conditions.

findings.finding_text: The cancellation liability window extends to a full 12 months with no-liability only beyond 365 days, and the sliding scale reaches 63-70% of room profit for cancellations 90 days or fewer out, exceeding what CD's fallback typically anticipates as a top tier. The 364-181 day tier at 35% and escalating bands compound Group's exposure across a very large block (210 rooms x 4 nights).
findings.cd_standard: Cancellation damages should be a sliding scale tied to proximity to the event, calculated against lost room profit, with no liability more than 12 months prior to arrival — but the top-tier percentage should not be materially higher than typical scales.
findings.proposed_language: Liquidated damages will be calculated as a percentage of room profit (defined as seventy percent (70%) of the confirmed group room rate) on a sliding scale not to exceed the following: 181-365 days, 25%; 91-180 days, 40%; 31-90 days, 50%; 30 days or fewer, 60%. No liability applies for cancellation more than twelve (12) months prior to arrival.
findings.exposure_basis: 210 rooms x 4 nights x $419/night x 70% top-tier damages rate for cancellations within 30 days of arrival

findings.finding_text: Menu pricing is locked 14 months prior to the event, exceeding CD's 12-month standard, and the shortfall billing rate is 40% of the difference (with Hotel retaining sole discretion to waive), both above and less favorable than CD's 35% shortfall standard.
findings.cd_standard: Menu pricing should be locked no earlier than 12 months before the event, and shortfall should be billed at 35% of the gap, not more.
findings.proposed_language: Menu prices for the Event's food and beverage functions will not be established earlier than twelve (12) months prior to the Event. If actual food and beverage revenue is less than the minimum, Group will pay Hotel thirty-five percent (35%) of the difference between actual revenue and the minimum.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel shall provide Group with a menu and pricing proposal at least fourteen (14) months prior to the Event date, and all menu selections and per-person pricing shall be locked and shall not be subject to increase or modification after that date.

findings.finding_text: While gratuity/service charge are separately disclosed as CD requires, the contract also imposes a strict 10-day dispute deadline after which charges are deemed accepted — a term not addressed by CD's standard and potentially limiting Group's ability to contest miscalculations.
findings.cd_standard: Gratuity and service charge should be clearly and separately defined and disclosed, without an unreasonably short deemed-acceptance window that could forfeit Group's right to dispute.
findings.proposed_language: Any dispute regarding the calculation or application of gratuity or service charge must be raised in writing within thirty (30) days of invoice receipt.
findings.quoted_text: Any dispute regarding the calculation or application of gratuity or service charge must be raised in writing within ten (10) days of invoice receipt, or the amounts shall be deemed accepted.

findings.finding_text: The finance charge on late undisputed balances is set at 1.3% per month, above CD's 1% (or legal maximum, whichever less) cap. The invoice dispute window is only 12 days, shorter than CD's 30-day standard, and prepayment absent credit approval is set at 75% versus CD's request for a defined, more moderate percentage.
findings.cd_standard: Finance charges on late undisputed balances should be capped at 1% per month or the legal maximum, whichever is less; Group should have 30 days to dispute charges before any finance charge accrues; and prepayment without credit approval should be a clearly defined, reasonable percentage.
findings.proposed_language: If payment of all undisputed charges is not received within thirty (30) days of the final invoice, a finance charge not to exceed one percent (1.0%) per month, or the maximum allowed by law, whichever is less, will apply to the unpaid, undisputed balance. Group will have thirty (30) days from receipt of the final itemized invoice to dispute any charge before any finance charge accrues. If credit is not approved, prepayment of no more than fifty percent (50%) of estimated charges will be required prior to arrival.
findings.quoted_text: The Monarch shall assess a monthly finance charge of 1.3% on any portion of an undisputed invoice balance remaining unpaid thirty (30) days after the invoice due date.

findings.finding_text: Indemnification is mutual and limited to each party's own negligence as CD requires, but the clause does not specify that each party's reasonable attorney's fees are recoverable as part of the indemnified damages from the indemnifying party's negligence beyond the general 'costs and expenses' language — this is a minor gap relative to CD's fuller standard language, and the $2.5M liability limit for a 210-room, 4-night event should be reviewed for proportionality.
findings.cd_standard: Indemnification should be mutual, limited to each party's own negligence, and expressly include each party's reasonable attorney's fees; insurance requirements should stay proportionate to event size.
findings.proposed_language: To the extent permitted by law, each party will protect, indemnify, defend, and hold harmless the other party and its employees, agents, and independent contractors against claims, losses, or damages to persons or property, and costs (including reasonable attorney's fees), arising out of the negligence or willful misconduct of the indemnifying party in connection with the Event.
findings.quoted_text: Each party shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless the other party, its officers, directors, employees, and agents from and against any and all claims, damages, liabilities, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees) arising out of or resulting from any breach of this Agreement by the indemnifying party, any injury to persons or damage to property caused by the indemnifying party, or any violation of law by the indemnifying party in connection with the Event.

findings.finding_text: The clause requires the parties to negotiate cost allocation for auxiliary aids in good faith rather than assigning Group responsibility for function-space aids and the Hotel responsibility for guest room/common area aids, leaving Group exposed to open-ended cost-sharing negotiations.
findings.cd_standard: Costs for auxiliary aids should be divided clearly: Group funds aids needed in its function space; Hotel funds aids required in guest rooms and common areas.
findings.proposed_language: Group is responsible for obtaining and funding any auxiliary aids needed in the function space held for its use; Hotel is responsible for obtaining and funding any auxiliary aids required by law in guest rooms, public space, and common areas.
findings.quoted_text: the cost of such auxiliary aids shall be divided between the Group and the Hotel... the parties shall negotiate in good faith to determine the appropriate allocation of costs for each specific auxiliary aid

findings.finding_text: Weekly pickup reports begin 8 weeks prior to the Event, and the reporting section does not specify a reservation pace report starting 90 days prior to cutoff, or that miscoded rooms occupied by registrants but not coded to Group will be credited to Group's pickup — a protection in CD's standard that is absent here.
findings.cd_standard: Group should receive a weekly pickup report, a full post-event report within 30 days including a pace report from 90 days prior to cutoff, and any guest occupying a room but miscoded should be credited to Group's pickup regardless of rate paid.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will provide Group a weekly guestroom pickup report starting ninety (90) days prior to the cutoff date, including a reservation pace report. Any guest room occupied by an individual on Group's registration list but not coded to Group within Hotel's system will be credited to Group's final pickup regardless of the rate paid.
findings.quoted_text: Beginning eight (8) weeks prior to the Event and continuing weekly through the cutoff date established in this Agreement, the Hotel shall provide Group with a written pickup report

findings.finding_text: Notice of collective bargaining agreement expirations is required only 9 months in advance, short of CD's standard of a full year's advance notice, marginally reducing Group's lead time to plan around potential labor disruption.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should give a year's advance notice of when its collective bargaining agreements expire.
findings.proposed_language: One year in advance, Hotel will provide Group in writing a list of all collective bargaining agreement expiration dates for the ensuing year.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel shall provide written notice to the Group of any expiration, non-renewal, or material breach in any collective bargaining agreement, union contract, or labor agreement covering employees at the Hotel no later than nine (9) months prior to the expiration date of such agreement.

findings.finding_text: Group's termination right for a brand/ownership/management change is conditioned on Group demonstrating in good faith that the change materially affects performance or alters service standards, rather than being available at Group's sole discretion as CD's standard calls for — this adds a burden of proof that could be disputed by the Hotel.
findings.cd_standard: The group should be able to terminate without liability within 30 days of notice of a change in ownership, management, or brand, without needing to prove material impact.
findings.proposed_language: Group may, at its sole discretion, terminate this Agreement without liability within thirty (30) days of receiving notice of a change in the Hotel's brand affiliation, management company, or ownership.
findings.quoted_text: The Group's termination right shall be conditioned upon the Group demonstrating, in good faith, that the change materially affects the Hotel's ability to perform its obligations under this Agreement or materially alters the character or service standards of the property.
findings.location_section: 18. Change of Brand, Management or Ownership

findings.finding_text: No deposit is charged, so the specific 30-day refund window and non-commingling protections in CD's standard are moot for a security deposit itself, but the contract also does not specify a defined refund timeline for any damage-related holdback beyond describing invoicing steps; no explicit 30-day refund guarantee for undisputed remaining deposit is stated except contingent on 'following such payment.'
findings.cd_standard: Any security or damage deposit should be refundable within a defined window (30 days is standard) absent documented, itemized damage.
findings.proposed_language: Any security deposit collected under this Agreement will be refunded in full within thirty (30) days of the event's conclusion unless the Hotel provides Group with an itemized accounting of specific, documented damage.

analysis.document_notes: Contract is well-organized with numbered sections closely tracking CD's standard clause categories, suggesting it was drafted with awareness of these issues but with terms shaded in the Hotel's favor at the margins (attrition threshold/rate, F&B lock-in timing and shortfall %, finance charge rate, dispute windows, cutoff days, CBA notice period, and ADA cost-sharing). No damage deposit is charged (Section 15), and no outside vendor surcharge is imposed (stated as $0.00 in Section 20), so those two provisions largely favor Group already. Rate parity, force majeure, named storm, termination for cause, walk/relocation, mandatory fees, complimentary rooms, attendee data, assignment, and governing law/venue clauses generally track CD's standard well. Two schedule references (Schedule A) were not included in the provided text; cancellation table appears to be reproduced directly in Section 4.
